name: io.github.Graphmaxer/gw1-mcp
title: Guild Wars 1 Build Compiler
description: GW1 build compiler: skill data, template code encode/decode, validation, hero roster. Read-only.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Look up a single GW1 skill by exact English or official French name, or by template skill id. Returns full stats (energy, activation, recharge, adrenaline, sacrifice), profession, attribute, campaign, elite flag and description. If the name is not found, returns the closest matches so you can correct spelling. Use this when you already know the exact skill; to discover skills by profession, attribute or name fragment, use search_skills instead.

name.description: Exact skill name, e.g. "Mystic Regeneration". The official French name also resolves ("Sceau de guérison" -> Healing Signet); build skill names accept it too; every other name field is English-only.

tools.name: search_skills
tools.description: Search the full GW1 skill database by profession, attribute, campaign, elite flag or name fragment (valid values are documented per parameter). Returns compact records, at most `limit` of them alongside a `total` count of every match — a full page is not the whole result, page with offset. Use get_skill for full details.

professionName.description: Filter by profession: Warrior, Ranger, Monk, Necromancer, Mesmer, Elementalist, Assassin, Ritualist, Paragon, Dervish, or None (common / PvE-only skills that belong to no profession).

attributeName.description: Filter by attribute line, exact English name, e.g. "Blood Magic", "Swordsmanship", "Divine Favor".

campaignName.description: Filter by the campaign a skill was INTRODUCED in: Core, Prophecies, Factions, Nightfall, or Eye of the North. Not a filter on availability — every attribute line spans several campaigns, so combining this with attributeName hides most of the line. Omit it when exploring an attribute.

elite.description: If true, return only elite skills; if false, only non-elite; omit for both.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the ENGLISH skill name, e.g. "heal" matches every skill with 'heal' in its name. A French substring matches nothing — use get_skill for a French name.

includePvpVersions.description: Include separate '(PvP)' skill versions. Default false — most builds want the PvE version only.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return (1–200, default 50). Narrow filters if you hit it.

offset.description: Number of records to skip, for paging through results beyond the limit.

tools.name: decode_template
tools.description: Decode an in-game GW1 skill template code (e.g. "OwpiMypMBg1cxcBAMBdmtIKAA") into professions, attribute allocations and the 8 skills with their stats and descriptions. Whitespace and line wraps in the pasted code are tolerated. This decodes a SINGLE build code; for a multi-hero paw-ned2 team blob, use decode_pawned_team instead.

tools.name: decode_pawned_team
tools.description: Decode a paw-ned2 team build blob (the 'pwnd0001...>...<' format shared on PvXwiki team pages and by the paw-ned2 tool) into its individual builds: player/hero label, description, and each skill bar fully decoded. Whitespace and line wraps in the pasted blob are tolerated. For a single (non-team) build code, use decode_template instead.

pwnd.description: The full pwnd blob, starting with 'pwnd000'

tools.name: encode_template
tools.description: Compile a build (professions, attributes, 8 skill names in English or French) into an official in-game template code. The build is validated first; on rule violations the errors are returned instead of a code. Unknown skill names return closest-match suggestions. IMPORTANT: template codes MUST come from this tool — never write or guess a code by hand, hand-written codes are invalid in-game. If unsure, verify any code with decode_template.

secondary.description: Secondary profession, e.g. "Monk". Omit or "None" for none.

attributes.description: Attribute point allocations (template format caps this at 15 entries)

skills.description: Exactly 8 official English or French skill names in bar order. Use null for an empty slot.

forHero.description: Set true if this bar is for a hero (PvE-only skills are errors)

forPvp.description: Set true for a PvP character's bar: PvE-only skills become errors. Never use '(PvP)' skill versions, even here: templates always carry the PvE id.

unlockedSkillIds.description: Optional: unlocked skill ids from a GWToolbox account export (/exportaccount): learnedCharacterSkills for a player bar, unlockedAccountSkills for a hero. Skills outside this list are flagged as warnings.

tools.name: validate_build
tools.description: Check a build (professions, attributes, 8 skill names in English or French) against Guild Wars 1 rules: one elite max, profession/attribute ownership, primary attributes, duplicates, rank ranges. Returns { valid, errors, warnings } without encoding — use encode_template instead when you also want the template code, since it runs these same rules and refuses on any error.

secondary.description: Secondary profession, e.g. "Monk". Omit or "None" for none.

attributes.description: Attribute point allocations (template format caps this at 15 entries)

skills.description: Exactly 8 official English or French skill names in bar order. Use null for an empty slot.

forHero.description: Set true if this bar is for a hero (PvE-only skills are errors)

forPvp.description: Set true for a PvP character's bar: PvE-only skills become errors. Never use '(PvP)' skill versions, even here: templates always carry the PvE id.

unlockedSkillIds.description: Optional: unlocked skill ids from a GWToolbox account export (/exportaccount): learnedCharacterSkills for a player bar, unlockedAccountSkills for a hero. Skills outside this list are flagged as warnings.

tools.name: get_hero
tools.description: Look up a GW1 hero by name or by id (GWCA HeroID, matching the AccountExport plugin output). Returns profession, campaign and how the hero is unlocked. Remember: heroes can equip any skill unlocked at ACCOUNT level, but NO PvE-only skill at all — including Signet of Capture. validate_build with forHero=true reports each one as an error, not a warning. Use this for one known hero; to browse or filter the roster, use list_heroes instead.

tools.name: list_heroes
tools.description: List all GW1 heroes, optionally filtered by profession or campaign name. Useful for team-building: shows which professions are coverable by heroes and how each hero is unlocked.

professionName.description: Filter by the hero's profession, exact English name: Warrior, Ranger, Monk, Necromancer, Mesmer, Elementalist, Assassin, Ritualist, Paragon or Dervish.

campaignName.description: Filter by the campaign the hero is recruited in, exact English name: Prophecies, Factions, Nightfall or Eye of the North.
